text:
RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 35

An all-male panel is, on its own, weak evidence. It's common in senior medical hierarchies and reflects who holds those posts — it doesn't show bias in your case. Leading with it will read as an accusation and let them dismiss the rest.

Your stronger ground is concrete: a PhD and eight years of section leadership versus a master's and a course, with the decisive criterion described only as "broad leadership experience" — vague, unquantified, and exactly the kind of wording that absorbs unexamined assumptions. Plus two weeks of silence on a reasonable request.

So: press for the written reasons and the scoring criteria first. Mention panel composition as context only if the explanation turns out to be thin or never arrives.
